The A1 dominance pass is a sub-pose margin that reverses held out. Frozen exact Bench(110,360), re-worn by this audit: plain 18.67 vs the lead's 18.91 (+0.24, i.e. 0.86 of one workspace pose at 0.278 points per pose); 2 mm 33.10 vs 34.03 (+0.93); 1 mm 20.30 vs 20.00 (-0.30). The whole plain gain is contact-pose count: 2 contact poses against 4 (contact 0.0054 vs 0.0107 = +0.53), offset by in-band14 0.8937 vs 0.8966 (-0.29). Reach is identical (261 of 360, overhead 8 of 28). Held out, with both designs re-worn through the same harness (alignment_audit remeasure): 23.73 vs 22.67 (-1.06; 851 vs 859 taken poses of 1154); 1 mm 26.83 vs 25.75 (-1.08); 2 mm 37.02 vs 37.24 (+0.22). Not gamed: at 3 mm this design is far ahead (107.65 vs 155.98 on the bench, 101.03 vs 163.09 held out; 133 vs 178 and 274 vs 427 poses under 3 mm). So the lead is not shown to be better for the wearer. But the gate's 'beats the lead' reading is noise, not a better exo, and it fails the 1-point rule. The drive sits at its transmission cap. The K stroke limit is set by the horn pressure angle (why_lim 'pressure_horn', dK_lim 46.2 deg). The taken dK reaches 45.62 deg, where the pressure angle reaches 43.0, exactly PA_MAX. That is the 2-degree cushion under the 45 gate, kept for the ~0.6 deg K slop and the flank tolerance. The tightest clearances are bent arm to hub K 1.14 mm and roller to hub K 2.02 mm. No force or dynamics check (R17) exists for this drive at that step, so the feel of a 43-degree roller-flank contact under K slop is unmeasured. The knee window walked toward the straight-knee singularity, but the score does not depend on it. ang_min has no bound anywhere in the model's _clamp chain, and the search moved it from the seed's 26.88 (the lead's verified value) to 25.22 (H1: 30.46). The taken knee angle runs to 151.92 deg on the bench and 153.16 held out, against the lead's 146.14 / 150.86: 5.8 deg closer to straight on the bench. Re-worn at the lead's ang_min 26.88, the result is identical (18.67 / 20.30 / 33.10), so the walk buys nothing against the lead. Re-worn at H1's 30.46: plain 18.71, 1 mm 20.36, 2 mm 36.76, reach 0.7167 (3 fewer poses), overhead 7 of 28. At that window it falls behind the lead at 2 mm. [evidence: docs/alignment/remeasure/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_angmin26.8823.json, docs/alignment/remeasure/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_angmin30.46.json, docs/alignment/live_audit_2026-10-16/probe_roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_th.json (knee_ang_taken 86.21-151.92, window 25.22-154.78), remeasure _held.json coord_spans K.ang 86.21-153.16; docs/concepts/models/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r.py:61-70]

K is scored at its planned (slaved) value, but it is held there by a single clock-spring cap that force-closes two rolling pairs: the lobe follower on hub 2's cap, and the MR63ZZ roller on the conjugate flank. The cam synthesis checks lift-off, cusp and pressure angles kinematically. No dynamics judge (R17) has run on this design, so nothing shows that the spring holds K on the law under arm load or gravity across the thorax. The new slaved-coordinate coupling in judge/dynamics.py (commits 5d6b819, 9f28755) is the instrument. This is required before any CAD, not before a screen.
